newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebels prepare to sweep through Colombian jungle.
newsitem.headline: Rebels prepare to sweep through Colombian jungle.

text.p: Hundreds of leftist guerrilla fighters will sweep through Colombia's southern jungle early on Wednesday to verify that government troops have pulled out as agreed, a rebel spokesman said.

President Ernesto Samper ordered the army to demilitarize a 5,000 square mile (13,000 sq km) area of Caqueta province to permit Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels to release the 60 soldiers they captured in combat nine months ago.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, a FARC spokesman said the rebel army was not seeking to turn the release of its captives into a political show and said the guerrillas would not destroy deserted military bases.

"FARC rebels will not be entering the zone, they are already there ... We're not looking to convert this into a political victory. We just want to hand over the soldiers and show the world that the FARC treats its prisoners in a dignified fashion," international spokesman Marco Leon Calarca told Reuters.
The FARC captured the 60 soldiers, and killed at least 27 others, when it overran a military base in neighbouring Putumayo province on Aug. 30, 1996.

The attack marked the start of one of the bloodiest rebel offensives in three decades of armed uprising and the beginning of Latin America's longest-running hostage crisis -- largely overshadowed by the recent siege of the Japanese embassy residence in Lima.
The FARC has said it will release 10 marines captured in a separate battle in northwest Choco province along with the soldiers.
Calarca declined to say how many rebels would patrol through the demilitarized zone but said it would be "many, many more" than the 400 that took part in the August attack in Putumayo.
By mid-afternoon on Tuesday, army commander Gen. Manuel Jose Bonett said the pullout of an estimated 5,000 troops had been completed ahead of schedule.
